items.informal_name: Total Degree in a Variable of a Product of Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_2} {n : σ} [inst : CommSemiring R] [NoZeroDivisors R] {ι : Type u_3} (s : Finset ι)
  (f : ι → MvPolynomial σ R),
  (∀ i ∈ s, f i ≠ 0) → MvPolynomial.degreeOf n (∏ i ∈ s, f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, MvPolynomial.degreeOf n (f i)
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ of indices and a function $ f $ assigning non-zero multivariate polynomials to each element of $ s $, the total degree of the product $ \prod_{i \in s} f(i) $ in the variable $ n $ is equal to the sum of the total degrees of each $ f(i) $ in $ n $, i.e., $ \deg_n\left(\prod_{i \in s} f(i)\right) = \sum_{i \in s} \deg_n(f(i)) $.

items.informal_name: Additivity of Total Degree in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_2} {n : σ} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p q : MvPolynomial σ R} [NoZeroDivisors R],
  p ≠ 0 → q ≠ 0 → MvPolynomial.degreeOf n (p * q) = MvPolynomial.degreeOf n p + MvPolynomial.degreeOf n q
items.informal_description: For non-zero multivariate polynomials $ p $ and $ q $, the total degree of their product in a variable $ n $ is equal to the sum of their individual total degrees in $ n $, i.e., $\deg_n(pq) = \deg_n(p) + \deg_n(q)$.

items.informal_name: Leading Monomial of Product Equals Sum Under Monomial Order
items.type:

  {P : ι → MvPolynomial σ R} {s : Finset ι}, (∀ i ∈ s, P i ≠ 0) → m.degree (∏ i ∈ s, P i) = ∑ i ∈ s, m.degree (P i)
items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $ with no zero divisors, a type $ \sigma $, and a finite set $ s $ of indices, if each polynomial $ P(i) $ for $ i \in s $ is non-zero, then the leading monomial of the product $ \prod_{i \in s} P(i) $ under a monomial order $ m $ is equal to the sum of the leading monomials of each $ P(i) $.

items.informal_name: Natural Degree of Product of Non-Zero Polynomials: $\deg\left(\prod_{i \in s} f(i)\right) = \sum_{i \in s} \deg f(i)$

items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, finite set $ s $, and function $ f : s \to R[X] $, if all $ f(i) $ are non-zero polynomials, then the natural degree of the product $ \prod_{i \in s} f(i) $ is equal to the sum of the natural degrees of each $ f(i) $, i.e., $ \deg\left(\prod_{i \in s} f(i)\right) = \sum_{i \in s} \deg(f(i)) $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Order of Product Equals Sum of Weighted Orders in Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [NoZeroDivisors R] [Nontrivial R] {ι : Type u_4} (w : σ → ℕ)
  (f : ι → MvPowerSeries σ R) (s : Finset ι),
  MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w (∏ i ∈ s, f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w (f i)
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $ with no zero divisors and nontrivial, the weighted order of the product of a finite set of multivariate power series over $ R $ with respect to a weight function $ w $ is equal to the sum of the weighted orders of each individual power series. Formally, for any finite set $ s $, $ \text{weightedOrder}_w\left(\prod_{i \in s} f_i\right) = \sum_{i \in s} \text{weightedOrder}_w(f_i) $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Homogeneity of Product of Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] {ι : Type u_4}
  (s : Finset ι) (φ : ι → MvPolynomial σ R) (n : ι → M) {w : σ → M},
  (∀ i ∈ s, MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w (φ i) (n i)) →
    MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w (∏ i ∈ s, φ i) (∑ i ∈ s, n i)
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative semiring, $ \sigma $ an index type for variables, and $ w : \sigma \to M $ a weight function taking values in an additive commutative monoid $ M $. If $ \{\varphi_i\}_{i \in s} $ is a finite family of multivariate polynomials in $ R[\sigma] $, each of which is weighted homogeneous of weight $ n_i $ with respect to $ w $, then their product $ \prod_{i \in s} \varphi_i $ is weighted homogeneous of weight $ \sum_{i \in s} n_i $ with respect to $ w $. This means every monomial in the product has weighted degree equal to the sum of the individual weights $ n_i $.

items.informal_name: Additivity of Weighted Order under Multiplication of Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] [NoZeroDivisors R] (w : σ → ℕ) (f g : MvPowerSeries σ R),
  MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w (f * g) = MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f + MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w g
items.informal_description: For a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $ and multivariate power series $ f, g $, the weighted order of the product $ f \cdot g $ with respect to $ w $ is equal to the sum of the weighted orders of $ f $ and $ g $ with respect to $ w $. Formally, $ \operatorname{weightedOrder}_w(fg) = \operatorname{weightedOrder}_w(f) + \operatorname{weightedOrder}_w(g) $.

items.informal_name: Product of Weighted Homogeneous Polynomials is Weighted Homogeneous with Combined Weights
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  {φ ψ : MvPolynomial σ R} {m n : M} {w : σ → M},
  MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w φ m →
    MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w ψ n → MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w (φ * ψ) (m + n)
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative semiring, $ \sigma $ an index type, and $ w : \sigma \to M $ a weight function. If $ \varphi $ and $ \psi $ are weighted homogeneous polynomials in $ R[\sigma] $ with weights $ m $ and $ n $ respectively (i.e., all monomials in $ \varphi $ have weighted degree $ m $ and all monomials in $ \psi $ have weighted degree $ n $), then their product $ \varphi \cdot \psi $ is a weighted homogeneous polynomial with weight $ m + n $. This means every monomial in $ \varphi \cdot \psi $ has weighted degree equal to the sum of the weights of $ \varphi $ and $ \psi $.

items.name: MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousComponent_apply
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] {w : σ → M} (n : M)
  (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) [inst_2 : DecidableEq M],
  (MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousComponent w n) φ =
    ∑ d ∈ φ.support with (Finsupp.weight w) d = n, (MvPolynomial.monomial d) (MvPolynomial.coeff d φ)

items.type:

items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a semiring, $ A $ an additive monoid, and $ T $ an ordered additive monoid with a degree function $ D : A \to T $. For any $ f, g \in R[A] $, the infimum degree of the product $ f \cdot g $ satisfies $ \inf\text{deg}(f \cdot g) \geq \inf\text{deg}(f) + \inf\text{deg}(g) $, where $ \inf\text{deg} $ denotes the infimum of the degrees of the support elements.

items.type:

  [inst_2 : CommSemiring R] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid A] [inst_4 : AddCommMonoid T] [AddLeftMono T] [AddRightMono T]
  {degt : A → T},
  0 ≤ degt 0 →

items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $ and an additive commutative monoid $ A $, let $ \text{degt} : A \to \mathbb{R} $ satisfy $ \text{degt}(0) \geq 0 $ and $ \text{degt}(a + b) \geq \text{degt}(a) + \text{degt}(b) $. For any finite set $ s $ and function $ f : s \to R[A] $, the sum of the infima of $ \text{degt} $ over the supports of each $ f(i) $ is less than or equal to the infimum of $ \text{degt} $ over the support of the product $ \prod_{i \in s} f(i) $.

items.informal_name: Subadditivity of Support Infimum under Multiplication in Additive Monoid Algebra
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} {T : Type u_4} [inst : SemilatticeInf T] [inst_1 : OrderTop T] [inst_2 : Semiring R]
  [inst_3 : Add A] [inst_4 : Add T] [AddLeftMono T] [AddRightMono T] {degt : A → T},
  (∀ (a b : A), degt a + degt b ≤ degt (a + b)) →
    ∀ (f g : AddMonoidAlgebra R A), f.support.inf degt + g.support.inf degt ≤ (f * g).support.inf degt
items.informal_description: For any subadditive degree function $\deg : A \to T$ on an additive monoid $A$, and for all elements $f, g$ in the additive monoid algebra $R[A]$, the sum of the infima of the supports of $f$ and $g$ under $\deg$ is less than or equal to the infimum of the support of their product $f \cdot g$ under $\deg$. Formally, $\inf_{\text{supp}(f)} \deg + \inf_{\text{supp}(g)} \deg \leq \inf_{\text{supp}(f \cdot g)} \deg$.
